translationRepairs: Na'erjing'e was dismissed and arrested; Gui Liang was made governor-general of Zhili and ordered, together with Grand Secretary Sengbao, to organize defense and pursuit without delay.
Na'erjing'e was dismissed and arrested; Gui Liang was made governor-general of Zhili and ordered, together with Banner Commander Shengbao, to organize defense and pursuit without delay.
都統 is Banner Commander, not Grand Secretary, and 勝保 is Shengbao.

Na'erjing'e was stripped of office and arrested for trial; Gui Liang was appointed governor-general of Zhili, and an edict rebuked him to join Grand Secretary Sengbao in swiftly planning defense and suppression.

Na'erjing'e was stripped of office and arrested for trial; Gui Liang was appointed governor-general of Zhili, and an edict rebuked him to join Banner Commander Shengbao in swiftly planning defense and suppression.
都統 is Banner Commander, not Grand Secretary, and 勝保 is Shengbao.

When censor Huang Juesi brought the matter to court, Gui Liang was ordered to investigate. He tore down the cult shrines and, on inquiry, found thirty-nine "Eternal Mother" temples across Henan and had them all demolished as well;

When censor Huang Juezi brought the matter to court, Gui Liang was ordered to investigate. He tore down the cult shrines and, on inquiry, found thirty-nine "Eternal Mother" temples across Henan and had them all demolished as well;
The name 黃爵滋 is romanized Huang Juezi, matching the source and supplied pinyin.

The rebels swept through Zhengding, Dingzhou, Shenzhou, Hejian, and Tianjin with great ferocity. Gui Liang held Baoding with Regional Commander Zhang Dianyuan; Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin camped at Tongzhou with the main army to shield the capital; and Sengbao led the pursuit.

The rebels swept through Zhengding, Dingzhou, Shenzhou, Hejian, and Tianjin with great ferocity. Gui Liang held Baoding with Regional Commander Zhang Dianyuan; Prince Senggelinqin of Horqin camped at Tongzhou with the main army to shield the capital; and Shengbao led the pursuit.
勝保 is Shengbao; Sengbao incorrectly conflates his name with Senggelinqin's.

In Xianfeng 4 the Qing won a major victory at Duliuzhen. The rebels withdrew to Fucheng, then to Lianzhen. Senggelinqin and Sengbao attacked jointly; when the rebels split and fled into Shandong, Sengbao pursued.

In Xianfeng 4 the Qing won a major victory at Duliuzhen. The rebels withdrew to Fucheng, then to Lianzhen. Senggelinqin and Shengbao attacked jointly; when the rebels split and fled into Shandong, Shengbao pursued.
Both appearances of 勝保 in this sentence name Shengbao.

After Senggelinqin's repeated defeats the enemy advanced on Tongzhou. Rui Lin and Sengbao met them at Baliqiao in a pincer attack, but Sengbao was wounded by cannon fire and thrown from his horse, the army collapsed, and the enemy pressed toward Beijing.

After Senggelinqin's repeated defeats the enemy advanced on Tongzhou. Rui Lin and Shengbao met them at Baliqiao in a pincer attack, but Shengbao was wounded by cannon fire and thrown from his horse, the army collapsed, and the enemy pressed toward Beijing.
Both appearances of 勝保 in this sentence name Shengbao.

Governor Jiang Yisui was reputed as a capable commander, and Rui Lin's generals Fang Yao and Zheng Shaozhong were skilled fighters. Together they crushed the Wukeng Hakka bandits, outlaws in Caochong, Chixi, Xin'an, and Dongguan, and pirates and bandits in Chaozhou and Qiongzhou.

Governor Jiang Yili was reputed as a capable commander, and Rui Lin's generals Fang Yao and Zheng Shaozhong were skilled fighters. Together they crushed the Wukeng Hakka bandits, outlaws in Caochong, Chixi, Xin'an, and Dongguan, and pirates and bandits in Chaozhou and Qiongzhou.
The name 蔣益澧 is Jiang Yili, matching the source and supplied pinyin.
I have ordered Luo Zundian with a hundred war junks to strike Hanyang from Xiantao and Caidian while Governor Yang Pi attacks from another direction;
I have ordered Luo Zundian with a hundred war junks to strike Hanyang from Xiantao and Caidian while Governor Yang Pei attacks from another direction;
The name 楊霈 is Yang Pei, matching the source and supplied pinyin.
In Xianfeng 5 Governor-General Yang Pi was routed at De'an. Hanyang and Hankou fell again, then De'an and Suizhou. Yang Pi was dismissed and Guan Wen was made governor-general of Huguang.
In Xianfeng 5 Governor-General Yang Pei was routed at De'an. Hanyang and Hankou fell again, then De'an and Suizhou. Yang Pei was dismissed and Guan Wen was made governor-general of Huguang.
Both appearances of 楊霈 in this sentence name Yang Pei.
